hints: Notice the cube has side $a$, so its volume is $a^3$, and its top face is at depth $h$ with its bottom face at depth $h+a$ in liquid of density $\rho_L$.
Recall that upthrust is the difference between the upward force on the bottom and the downward force on the top, or equivalently the weight of displaced liquid.
Check whether the result should depend on $\rho_L$ or $\rho_w$, and whether depth $h$ cancels when you subtract the two pressure forces.
walkthrough: Volume of the fully immersed cube is $V = a \times a \times a = a^3$.
By Archimedes principle, upthrust $U$ equals weight of liquid displaced: $U = \rho_L V g$.

The same result follows from pressure difference: top force $= \rho_L g h a^2$ downward and bottom force $= \rho_L g (h+a) a^2$ upward, so difference $= \rho_L g a^3$. Depth $h$ cancels and wood density $\rho_w$ is not used.

options.A: Upthrust equals weight of displaced liquid, $\rho_L \times a^3 \times g$ for the fully immersed cube.
options.B: This is the weight of the wooden block, $\rho_w a^3 g$, not the weight of displaced liquid which causes upthrust.
options.C: This omits the block area $a^2$ and uses depth $h$, giving wrong units and confusing pressure at the top with pressure difference.
options.D: This has units of force per unit area and omits $a^2$, so it cannot equal the total upthrust force on volume $a^3$.
